text:
[LCST.4.5.5] **`String → Bool` accepted inputs.** `x::Bool?` parses exactly the NFC strings
`"true"` and `"false"` (case-sensitive) to the corresponding `Bool`; any other value yields
`null`.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_5__parse_bool
idris.note: `String :: Bool?`: exactly the texts `true` and `false`, case-sensitive, to the Bool; nothing for any other text, which `lnul_8_4__parsed` makes `null`. The two texts are ASCII, so NFC changes nothing.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_5__parse_is_a_value_or_null
idris.note: For every text, `s :: Bool?` is a Bool or `null`, never a trap.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_6__bool_round_trip
idris.note: [LCST.4.5.6]'s Bool render parses back to its Bool, for both.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_6__render_bool
idris.note: `Bool :: String`: `true` / `false`, the inverse of this clause's parse.
